title: Deleted photos aren't really gone: Recently Deleted keeps them 30 days
caption:
Deleted photos aren't really gone. Your iPhone keeps them in Recently Deleted for 30 days, and Google Photos keeps its trash 30 days too.
Here's when a photo is really gone, and the copy you can't delete.
Is your Recently Deleted empty? Yes or no.
keywords: how to permanently delete photos on iphone
pinned_comment: Apple Support (Mar 31, 2026): deleted photos "go to your Recently Deleted album for 30 days." Google Photos Help: they "stay in your trash for 30 days before they are permanently deleted." To really delete on iPhone: Photos › swipe up › Recently Deleted › unlock › Select › More › Delete All. Google Photos: Collections › Trash › More › Empty Trash. How many are still sitting in yours?

pinned_backups.if: Can a recovery app get them back?
pinned_backups.reply: We only go as far as Apple's and Google's own pages. Apple: "When you delete a photo or video from this album, you can't get it back." Google: "Photos and videos that were permanently deleted can't be restored." We didn't test recovery tools, so the video makes no claim about them either way.

pinned_backups.if: What about photos I texted someone?
pinned_backups.reply: We found no Apple or Google page on that, so the video sticks to shared albums, where Apple says photos a friend saved "stay in your library even if the shared album is deleted or the person who created it stops sharing it."

Google's help page says it "details the current retention policy," and it now reads: "Photos and videos that you delete will stay in your trash for 30 days before they are permanently deleted." We went by the live page, read Nov 9, 2026.

pinned_backups.if: If I delete it on my iPhone, is it gone from my iPad too?
pinned_backups.reply: With iCloud Photos, yes. Apple: "When you use iCloud Photos and delete a photo or video on one device, it gets deleted on all other devices where you're signed in with the same Apple Account." It still goes to Recently Deleted first.

You may still have time. Apple: "If you accidentally deleted a photo or video, you can recover it within 30 days in the Recently Deleted album." Google: "You can only restore photos and videos if they're still in your trash."

pinned_backups.if: Why does it ask for Face ID?
pinned_backups.reply: Apple: "In iOS 16, iPadOS 16.1, or later, Face ID or Touch ID is required to view the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums by default." To turn that off: "Open the Settings app. Tap Apps, then tap Photos. Turn off Use Face ID."

youtube_description:
Deleted photos aren't really gone, at least not right away. On iPhone, hitting delete only moves a photo to the Recently Deleted album, Google Photos keeps it in the trash, and a copy a friend saved from your shared album stays with them.

Check yours. Apple Support: "Open the Photos app, swipe up, then tap Recently Deleted in the Utilities section." ("How to recover deleted photos on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple Vision Pro", published Sep 15, 2025)

Thirty days, locked. Apple Support, "Delete photos on your iPhone or iPad" (published Mar 31, 2026): "When you delete photos and videos, they go to your Recently Deleted album for 30 days. After 30 days, they'll be permanently deleted." And: "In iOS 16, iPadOS 16.1, or later, Face ID or Touch ID is required to view the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums by default." To turn the lock off: "Open the Settings app. Tap Apps, then tap Photos. Turn off Use Face ID."

Google Photos too. Google Photos Help, "Delete photos & videos": "Photos and videos that you delete will stay in your trash for 30 days before they are permanently deleted." And: "If you delete a photo or video that's backed up in Google Photos, it will stay in your trash for 30 days."

A friend's copy. Apple Support, "How to use Shared Albums in Photos on your iPhone, iPad, or Apple Vision Pro" (published Oct 6, 2026): "Any photos that you saved or downloaded from a shared album to your Photos library stay in your library even if the shared album is deleted or the person who created it stops sharing it."

To really delete it. iPhone: Photos › swipe up › Recently Deleted, unlock it, tap Select, then "Tap the More button, then tap Delete or Delete All." Apple: "When you delete a photo or video from this album, you can't get it back." Google Photos: Collections › Trash › More › Empty Trash › Delete permanently. Google: "When you empty your trash, you permanently delete any photos and videos in your trash, and they can't be restored."

Deleted one by accident? Apple: "If you accidentally deleted a photo or video, you can recover it within 30 days in the Recently Deleted album." Google: "You can only restore photos and videos if they're still in your trash."

So, is yours empty? Yes or no.

Fine print: "still here" means photos deleted in the last 30 days that you haven't emptied out. The lock is on by default in iOS 16 and later, and you can turn it off. The friend's copy covers photos saved from a shared album only; we found no Apple or Google page on photos you texted or sent another way, so the video makes no claim about them. "You can't get it back" is what Apple and Google say about their own apps; this video makes no claim about recovery tools. With iCloud Photos, Apple says: "When you use iCloud Photos and delete a photo or video on one device, it gets deleted on all other devices where you're signed in with the same Apple Account." Google says items you delete in Google Photos aren't automatically removed from Blogger, Drive, Gmail or YouTube, and "Deleted photos and videos might stay on a removable memory card." Other gallery apps aren't covered. The phones, albums and confirm screens in the video are re-created and drawn by hand; no real interface or logo is shown. Not sponsored by or affiliated with Apple or Google.
